svg.title: Layered PII detection, and the three places redaction applies differently
svg.desc: A hand-drawn figure. Three detection layers run cheapest first: regex and format rules catch structured PII such as card numbers with a Luhn check, national identifiers, emails, and phone numbers, fast and deterministic; named-entity recognition catches unstructured PII such as names, locations, and organisations using a small cheap model; and an LLM classifier catches the context-dependent cases the first two miss, slower and costlier so reserved for high-risk paths. A highlighted band names the tradeoff: redacting "email John Smith at john at acme dot com" into typed placeholders leaves the model unable to do the job, because the task was the PII. Three panels then separate where redaction applies: into the context only when the model does not need the data, into the trace store by policy on the fields a regulation names, and preferably as reversible tokenisation with the mapping held in an access-controlled vault.
svg.text: Detection layers cheapest first, and redaction is a scalpel
Three techniques in increasing cost, and one genuine conflict with the observability advice to keep the prompt.
Detection, cheapest first
Regex and format rules
Structured PII: card numbers with a Luhn
check, national identifiers, emails, phone
numbers.
Fast, deterministic, high precision on any
format carrying a checksum.
Named-entity recognition
Unstructured PII: person names, locations,
organisations.
A small model does this well and cheaply.
Presidio packages both this and the regex
layer.
An LLM classifier
The context-dependent cases the first two
miss: "the patient", "her account
balance".
Slower and costlier, so it is a fallback for
high-risk paths rather than the default.
Redaction replaces a span with a typed placeholder rather than deleting it, so the surrounding text still parses and the mapping can be reversed inside the boundary.
The tradeoff: redaction can destroy the task
"email John Smith at john@acme.com" becomes "email <PERSON_1> at <EMAIL_1>" — and the model can no longer do the job,
because the task was the PII.
Into the context
Only when the model genuinely does not need the
PII. A good default for a free-text upload
feeding a summary; a bad one when the task is
about the person.
Into the trace store
By policy, applied selectively to the fields a
regulation actually names. You trade some
debugging value for it, knowingly.
Prefer tokenisation
Swap the value for a reversible token; keep the
mapping in a tightly access-controlled vault.
Referential structure survives; the raw value
does not spread.
